tunables.label: API Server Enabled
tunables.description: Starts the OpenAI-compatible API server as a gateway platform adapter; it serves GET /health on port 8642.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without API_SERVER_ENABLED=true nothing listens on 8642 and the /health probe fails. The container must also be started with `gateway run` so the gateway daemon (which supervises the API server adapter) is running.

tunables.label: API Server Bind Address
tunables.description: Host/bind address for the API server; containers must bind 0.0.0.0 to accept published traffic.
tunables.troubleshooting: The upstream default 127.0.0.1 is unreachable from outside the container — set 0.0.0.0 and publish port 8642. API_SERVER_KEY is still required even on loopback binds.

tunables.label: API Server Key
tunables.description: Bearer token clients send to the API server; upstream refuses to start the API server without a strong key (minimum 16 characters).
tunables.troubleshooting: Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The key must be at least 16 characters or the API server refuses to start. The example is a local-only dummy value for compose validation — replace it before any real deployment.

tunables.label: Hermes Home
tunables.description: Persistent Hermes configuration, state and data directory; must point at the mounted volume (/opt/data).
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep it on the declared /opt/data volume so gateway/API state survives `docker compose down -v` rebuilds; a different path loses profile and provider state.

tunables.label: Unbuffered Python
tunables.description: Writes Python stdout/stderr without buffering so logs appear immediately.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set to true when container logs look delayed or truncated in `docker compose logs`.

tunables.label: Disable Bytecode Files
tunables.description: Prevents Python from writing .pyc bytecode files into the container filesystem.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep true in read-only or ephemeral root filesystems to avoid write errors on import.

tunables.label: Safe Write Root
tunables.description: Root directory that Hermes is allowed to write to (safe-write guard).
tunables.troubleshooting: Must stay inside the mounted /opt/data volume; writes outside this root are rejected.

tunables.label: Disable Lazy Installs
tunables.description: Disables on-demand package installs so container startup stays deterministic.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave enabled in containers; disabling allows installs at runtime into HERMES_LAZY_INSTALL_TARGET, which needs network and a writable volume.

tunables.label: API Server Port
tunables.description: Port the OpenAI-compatible API server listens on; must match the published container port.
tunables.troubleshooting: If the /health probe times out after changing this, update the compose mapping (for example 8643:8643) so both halves match, and keep probes pointed at the same port.

tunables.label: Anthropic API Key
tunables.description: Anthropic Console API key used when the active model provider is `anthropic`.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without it Hermes falls back to OAuth credentials (Claude Code files / `hermes model`) or the next configured provider; a 401 from api.anthropic.com means the key is missing or expired. Pair with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL only when routing through a proxy.

tunables.label: Anthropic Base URL
tunables.description: Overrides the Anthropic API base URL, for gateways or corporate proxies.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave unset for direct Anthropic access; a wrong path (missing `/v1`) yields 404s on every Anthropic request.

tunables.label: OpenAI API Key
tunables.description: API key for OpenAI or any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint used together with OPENAI_BASE_URL.
tunables.troubleshooting: Only read when `model.provider` selects an OpenAI-compatible provider; a 401 from the endpoint means the key is missing or the provider is misconfigured.

tunables.label: OpenAI Base URL
tunables.description: Base URL for a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, local gateway).
tunables.troubleshooting: Point at the `/v1` root; a wrong host or missing `/v1` shows up as connection errors or 404s on completion requests.

tunables.label: OpenRouter API Key
tunables.description: OpenRouter API key; upstream recommends it for access to many models through one credential.
tunables.troubleshooting: Select the provider with `hermes model`; a 401 from openrouter.ai means the key is missing, expired, or has no credit.

tunables.label: Google AI Studio API Key
tunables.description: Google AI Studio API key for Gemini models; GEMINI_API_KEY is an alias for this variable.
tunables.troubleshooting: Vertex AI does not use this key — it needs VERTEX_CREDENTIALS_PATH (service-account JSON) instead. A 403 usually means the key lacks Generative Language API access.

tunables.label: Gemini API Key
tunables.description: Alias for GOOGLE_API_KEY; used interchangeably by the Google/Gemini provider.
tunables.troubleshooting: Setting only one of GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY is enough; if both are set, keep them identical to avoid confusing provider diagnostics.

tunables.label: DeepSeek API Key
tunables.description: DeepSeek API key for direct DeepSeek access.
tunables.troubleshooting: Override DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL when using a relay; a 402/429 from DeepSeek means account balance or rate limits, not a container problem.

tunables.label: Groq API Key
tunables.description: Groq API key; upstream consumes it for Groq Whisper speech-to-text (and Groq-backed model access).
tunables.troubleshooting: Voice features stay silent without it — set STT_GROQ_MODEL only if you also need a non-default model (`whisper-large-v3-turbo` is the default).

tunables.label: xAI API Key
tunables.description: xAI (Grok) API key for chat, TTS and web search.
tunables.troubleshooting: xAI_BASE_URL defaults to https://api.x.ai/v1; only override it for a proxy. A 401 means the key is missing or the project has no credits.

tunables.label: Telegram Bot Token
tunables.description: Telegram bot token from @BotFather; enables the Telegram gateway adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without a token the gateway skips Telegram entirely. If the bot is added to groups but stays silent, also set TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS (and TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS for forums).

tunables.label: Telegram Allowed Users
tunables.description: Comma-separated Telegram user IDs allowed to use the bot in DMs, groups and forums.
tunables.troubleshooting: Unset, the bot does not accept anyone (except with TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS, which is dev-only). Get your numeric user ID from @userinfobot; never use allow-all on a public deployment.

tunables.label: Discord Bot Token
tunables.description: Discord bot token; enables the Discord gateway adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: A 4001/invalid-token error means the token was reset in the Developer Portal. The bot also needs the Message Content intent enabled in Discord, otherwise messages arrive empty.

tunables.label: Discord Allowed Users
tunables.description: Comma-separated Discord user IDs allowed to use the bot (DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES grants access by role instead).
tunables.troubleshooting: Messages are ignored until at least one user, role or channel is allowed; DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS exists for development only.

tunables.label: Slack Bot Token
tunables.description: Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) used by the Slack adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: Slack runs in Socket Mode, so this must be paired with SLACK_APP_TOKEN (`xapp-...`); without the app token the adapter cannot open its connection.

tunables.label: Slack App Token
tunables.description: Slack app-level token (`xapp-...`) required for Socket Mode.
tunables.troubleshooting: Generate it with `connections:write` scope on the Slack app; a `xapp_`/`xoxb_` mix-up is the usual cause of a failed handshake.

tunables.label: Slack Allowed Users
tunables.description: Comma-separated Slack user IDs allowed to trigger the bot.
tunables.troubleshooting: Unset, the bot only responds where SLACK_ALLOW_ALL_USERS or free-response channel rules apply; find IDs with `slack users list`.

tunables.label: Enable Web Dashboard
tunables.description: Starts the supervised web dashboard service (default port 9119) inside the container.
tunables.troubleshooting: Unset/`false`, the s6 dashboard service stays down — nothing listens on 9119. Publish port 9119 in compose and configure an auth provider (HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_*) before exposing a non-loopback bind.

tunables.label: Dashboard Bind Address
tunables.description: Bind address for the dashboard HTTP server.
tunables.troubleshooting: A loopback bind is unreachable from outside the container; keep 0.0.0.0 for published traffic and gate access with basic auth or OAuth.

tunables.label: Dashboard Port
tunables.description: Port for the dashboard HTTP server; must match the published container port.
tunables.troubleshooting: If the dashboard URL is unreachable, confirm the compose mapping (for example 9119:9119) matches this value and that HERMES_DASHBOARD=1 is set.

tunables.label: Dashboard Basic Auth Username
tunables.description: Username for the bundled username/password dashboard-auth provider; activates it when set together with a password.
tunables.troubleshooting: Setting only the username is a no-op — both HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME and a password (or password hash) are required before the auth gate turns on.

tunables.label: Dashboard Basic Auth Password
tunables.description: Plaintext password for the dashboard basic-auth provider (hashed in memory at load); wins over a configured password_hash so it can be rotated via env.
tunables.troubleshooting: The example is a local-only placeholder — replace it before any real deployment. Basic auth is suitable for a trusted LAN/VPN only; use HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID for public exposure. Sessions also need HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET to survive restarts.

tunables.label: Runtime User ID
tunables.description: Host UID the s6 stage2 hook remaps the internal `hermes` user to before services start; matches ownership of the mounted /opt/data volume.
tunables.troubleshooting: Permission errors on the mounted volume mean this does not match the host directory owner — run `id -u` on the host and set it (or PUID) on every container start, including throwaway diagnostic containers.

tunables.label: Runtime Group ID
tunables.description: Host GID paired with HERMES_UID for remapping the internal `hermes` group.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep it consistent with the host group of /opt/data (`id -g`); a mismatch shows up as group-readable-but-not-writable files after a rebuild.

tunables.label: Runtime User ID (alias)
tunables.description: Alias for HERMES_UID, provided for parity with LinuxServer.io and NAS images.
tunables.troubleshooting: If both are set, prefer HERMES_UID so there is one source of truth; either one prevents the UID-10000-takes-over-the-volume failure mode.

tunables.label: Runtime Group ID (alias)
tunables.description: Alias for HERMES_GID, provided for parity with LinuxServer.io and NAS images.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set it together with PUID; leaving GID unmapped on a group-owned volume reproduces the same permission errors as an unmatched UID.

notes: Ports: 8642 is the API server (API_SERVER_PORT default 8642, health endpoint GET /health); 9119 is the optional web dashboard started by the s6 dashboard service when HERMES_DASHBOARD=1 (HERMES_DASHBOARD_PORT default 9119), which requires an auth provider on non-loopback binds. The sample maps only the API port 8642. Provider credentials and messaging tokens are read from the process environment or `~/.hermes/.env` (prefer `config.yaml` for non-secret behaviour); every credential in `tunables` is optional, carries a placeholder example only, and none is supplied by the sample.
